features.name: meridian_web
features.tagline: The browser renderer — a ComponentKit of vanilla + React components that draws meridian descriptors as native DOM, bundled to the CDN.

hero.headline: Descriptors, drawn in the browser.
hero.subhead: meridian_web turns a PanelDescriptor into real DOM — forms, tables, launchpad, conversation — via a ComponentKit shared with meridian-mui-kit. The console's panels are all descriptors; nothing is a bespoke page.

meta.title: meridian_web — the browser renderer | meridian-ux
meta.description: meridian_web is the browser renderer for meridian-ux: a ComponentKit of vanilla + React components that draws meridian.ui.v1 descriptors as native DOM, re-skinned via meridian.theme.v1 and bundled to the CDN.

sections.title: One descriptor in, native DOM out.
sections.subtitle: The renderer routes on the panel body oneof and drives the shared interaction core.

steps.title: Route
steps.text: A PanelDescriptor arrives; the renderer routes on its body oneof (form / table / launchpad / conversation / …) to a ComponentKit component.

steps.title: Bind
steps.text: RpcInvoker maps the descriptor's RPCs to the host transport; FieldBindings wire inputs to the request.

steps.title: Skin
steps.text: applyTheme(meridian.json) sets the CSS custom properties — the same Theme every other renderer reads.

features.name: meridian-swift
features.tagline: The native renderer — the macOS dashboard and iOS console draw the same descriptors as first-class SwiftUI views.

hero.headline: The same descriptors, natively Apple.
hero.subhead: meridian-swift renders meridian.ui.v1 as real SwiftUI — grouped inset forms, native tables, native navigation, native toggles. No web view, no bridge: a form is a Form, a table is a List.

meta.title: meridian-swift — the native macOS + iOS renderer | meridian-ux
meta.description: meridian-swift is the native renderer for meridian-ux: the macOS dashboard and iOS console draw meridian.ui.v1 descriptors as first-class SwiftUI views, re-skinned via meridian.theme.v1 — no web view, no bridge.

highlights: Grouped inset forms, native tables + navigation
Drives the same shared interaction core as web + TUI
Decodes the meridian.theme.v1 binpb for palette + metrics
Ships in the macOS dashboard + the iOS console (TestFlight)

sections.title: Native fidelity, zero re-authoring.
sections.subtitle: A descriptor authored for the web console renders as a proper Settings-style screen on iOS with no new UI code.

callout.text: A BooleanToggle is a native UISwitch; an EnumSelection is a native disclosure row; a nested form is a native sub-screen — all decoded from the same proto the browser reads.

features.name: meridian_tui
features.tagline: The terminal renderer — forms, tables, launchpad, and conversation in the shell, from the same protos, keyboard-native, over SSH.

hero.headline: The whole console, in the terminal.
hero.subhead: meridian_tui renders meridian.ui.v1 with ratatui — box-drawn forms with checkbox toggles and enum spinners, colored-glyph status tables, a ⌘K launchpad, and block-kit conversation. Keyboard-native, SSH-friendly, same descriptors.

meta.title: meridian_tui — the terminal renderer | meridian-ux
meta.description: meridian_tui is the terminal renderer for meridian-ux: forms, tables, launchpad, and conversation drawn with ratatui from the same meridian.ui.v1 descriptors — keyboard-native, over SSH, re-skinned via meridian.theme.v1.

highlights: Box-drawn forms: checkbox toggles, f64 spinners, enum pickers
Drives the uiview-core shared cores (filter · model)

sections.title: The terminal filters the same as the browser.
sections.subtitle: The TUI drives the same Rust cores the wasm renderer ships, so ranking and dedupe agree across modalities.

callout.text: filter_launchpad and the ConversationModel are the Rust twins of the web's filter.ts and model.ts — the TUI renders, it doesn't re-implement, so a launchpad ranks identically in the shell and in the browser.

features.name: meridian_uiview_core
features.tagline: The portable core — Rust compiled to wasm (uiview), shipping the shared interaction logic the web and TUI renderers both drive.

hero.headline: One core, every language.
hero.subhead: meridian_uiview_core is the Rust heart of meridian — compiled to wasm. It holds the interaction logic (filter, model, validation) as the single source of truth the renderers drive, so behavior can't fork between surfaces.

meta.title: meridian_uiview_core — the portable Rust/wasm core | meridian-ux
meta.description: meridian_uiview_core is the portable Rust core of meridian-ux, compiled to wasm (uiview): the shared interaction logic — filter, model, validation — the web and TUI renderers both drive, so behavior agrees by construction.

highlights: Rust cores: launchpad filter · conversation model · form validation
Compiles to wasm for the web and links into the TUI
Rust ⇄ TypeScript twins agree by construction

sections.title: Renderers draw. They don't decide.
sections.subtitle: Ranking, validation, upsert, and dedupe live once — the behavior a user feels, shared across every surface.

callout.text: A renderer only turns state into pixels. Because the decisions live in one wasm-shared core, adding a fifth surface means writing a renderer, not re-deriving how a launchpad ranks or a form validates.
